top5.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
top5.description: CrowdStrike announced the all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing together endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security and threat intelligence. Jay Chaudhry will remain CEO of Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.
top5.why: CrowdStrike’s $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler would reshape the cybersecurity market by combining endpoint, cloud, zero-trust and threat-intelligence capabilities.

top5.title: The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
top5.description: Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.
top5.why: The EU Chips Act is unlocking €33 billion across more than 20 semiconductor projects, signaling a major push to reduce Europe’s dependence on foreign chip supply.

top5.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist calls for limiting the pace of AI progress
top5.description: Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores for every major model since GPT-3.5 and is asking competing labs to agree on common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.
top5.why: OpenAI’s chief scientist is calling for common limits on the pace of AI progress, potentially influencing industry coordination, safety policy and future regulation.

top5.title: Nvidia’s competitors are designing chips with artificial intelligence
top5.description: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are using AI models to design chips that could replace Nvidia GPUs. This development poses a significant risk to the company’s dominance.
top5.why: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are using AI to design chips that could improve their bargaining power and challenge Nvidia’s dominance in AI hardware.

top5.title: Microsoft’s massive outage exposes testing and capacity weaknesses
top5.description: Microsoft’s final report says a Windows defect went unnoticed for months before overwhelming Microsoft 365 gateway servers. More than 80% of North American gateway servers stopped responding at the height of the outage.
top5.why: Microsoft’s outage, which took more than 80% of North American gateway servers offline, exposes the operational and capacity risks of widely deployed cloud infrastructure.
